textTitles: Fire evacuation: what staff and wardens do

texts.label: A
texts.title: Fire evacuation: what staff and wardens do

paragraphs.text: Fire evacuation: what staff and wardens do. Every floor of the building has at least two fire wardens, whose names and photographs are displayed beside the lifts. Wardens are volunteers who receive half a day of training when they take on the role and a shorter refresher every year. The company aims to have enough wardens for at least one to be present on every floor throughout working hours, so staff who work part-time or on shifts are particularly encouraged to volunteer.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: When the alarm sounds as a continuous ringing, all staff must leave at once by the nearest exit and go to the assembly point in the car park opposite the main entrance. Do not stop to collect personal belongings, and do not use the lifts. If you are with visitors, you are responsible for taking them with you. An intermittent alarm, which sounds as a series of short rings, is a warning only: stay where you are, end any telephone calls and wait for an announcement.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Wardens have three tasks during an evacuation. They check the toilets, kitchens and meeting rooms on their floor, closing doors as they go; they help anyone who needs assistance to reach an exit or a refuge area on the stairs; and they report to the chief warden at the assembly point, confirming that their floor is clear. Wardens should not try to put out a fire unless it is very small and they have been trained to use the extinguisher, and they must never put themselves at risk.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Staff who might need help to leave the building, for example because of an injury or a condition that affects their movement, should ask their manager for a personal evacuation plan. The plan is agreed with the facilities team and reviewed whenever the person’s needs change. The whole building is evacuated for practice twice a year, at times that are not announced in advance, and the time taken to clear it is recorded and shared with all staff.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: The staff suggestion scheme. Anyone who works for the company, including temporary staff and those on fixed-term contracts, may put forward an idea for saving money, improving safety or making the working day easier. Suggestions are made through a form on the staff website; paper forms can be left in the box in the canteen by people who do not use a computer at work. Ideas may be submitted by an individual or by a team of up to four people.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Each suggestion is acknowledged within five working days and then passed to the manager of the department it would affect most. That manager has one month to assess it and to recommend whether it should be adopted, tried out on a small scale or rejected. A panel of five staff, chosen from different departments and changed every year, meets every two months to make the final decisions and to agree any awards.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Awards depend on the value of the idea. A suggestion that is adopted but brings no measurable saving receives a voucher worth £50. Where a saving can be measured, the person or team receives ten per cent of the first year’s saving, up to a limit of £5,000. Suggestions about safety are not given cash awards, because the company does not want safety matters to be delayed while savings are calculated; instead, the best safety idea each year receives a special certificate and an extra day of paid leave.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Some ideas cannot be considered. These include complaints about individual colleagues, which should be raised with a manager, and suggestions that simply repeat existing policy. An idea that has already been put forward by someone else within the previous two years will not receive an award, even if it is adopted, although the second person will be told that the idea was a good one. Anyone who is unhappy with the way their suggestion was handled may ask for it to be reviewed by the head of human resources.
paragraphs.label: D
